root_idea.summary: The root centers on one thing taking the place of another, extending to substitution, exchange, and change or alteration even when no replacement is supplied.
root_idea.development: The evidence distinguishes alteration without replacement from supplying or taking a substitute. From the same orientation develop reciprocal exchange, becoming changed, and technical or occupational uses involving substitution.

senses.definition: To change or alter a thing—its wording, form, quality, condition, or state—without necessarily replacing its substance.
senses.usage_conditions: Transitive; may describe alteration of a statement, form, quality, or condition while the underlying thing remains. The result may be expressed as a changed state or wording.

senses.definition: To replace one thing with another, putting the latter in its place; to give or change one thing for another.
senses.usage_conditions: Used with constructions meaning into, for, in place of, or in exchange for. It may be doubly transitive when both the replaced item and the replacement or resulting state are specified.

senses.definition: To provide or put a substitute in place of something; to replace or give one thing in exchange for another.
senses.usage_conditions: Typically takes the item replaced and the substitute or replacement; the construction may express giving someone a different person or thing in place of the former.

senses.definition: To exchange or adopt one thing in place of another.
senses.usage_conditions: The reciprocal or reflexive form is used for exchanging, taking one thing instead of another, or adopting a replacement; the relevant object may be expressed directly or with a preposition.

senses.definition: To take a substitute or replacement for one thing; to exchange it for another or take another in its place.
senses.usage_conditions: Commonly construed with بِـ, بِهِ, or مَكَانَ to identify the replacement or the thing whose place is taken.

senses.definition: A substitute, replacement, or thing put, given, or received instead of another; an exchange or compensation.
senses.usage_conditions: Denotes what stands in the place of another thing or person, including what is accepted in lieu of it.

senses.definition: One who changes or alters a thing.
senses.usage_conditions: An active participle of Form II; in Quranic usage it refers to an agent capable of altering an established word or decree.

senses.definition: Changing or altering; an alteration of a thing from one state, form, or condition to another.
senses.usage_conditions: A verbal noun of Form II. In Quranic usage it commonly occurs in negated or restricted constructions concerning divine words, creation, established practice, or a settled order.

senses.definition: Taking a substitute; replacing or exchanging one thing for another.
senses.usage_conditions: A verbal noun of Form X, denoting the act of taking something in place of something else.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Exchange or substitution: making one thing a substitute for another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical extension of the verbal noun that specifically emphasizes removal of the first substance and putting another in its place, rather than alteration without replacement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Reciprocal exchange, in which each party gives the other the like of what it takes or receives.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used for an exchange with another person or group, including exchanging equivalent garments, goods, or persons.
An inchoative use describing a thing that undergoes change, rather than the Quranic exchange construction represented under the Form V entry.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The “substitutes”: a class of righteous persons regarded as taking the place of others who have passed away.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical religious usage reported in Classical Arabic lexicography; the singular is related to بَدَلٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Letters of substitution: letters used in place of other letters.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A grammatical and orthographic technical term, excluding letters changed merely through assimilation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Generous and noble, when applied to a man.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival use that lexicographers connect with the idea of a substitute or one who takes another’s place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A dealer who continually exchanges one commodity or possession for another; specifically, a seller of provisions of various kinds.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is explained through changing one sale for another and may also describe someone whose limited property is successively sold and exchanged for new goods.

cautions: The Quranic uses of بَدَّلَ and تَبْدِيلٌ preserve a distinction between alteration and replacement, although English translations may render both with “change.” The construction and whether a replacement is supplied determine the more specific sense.
